translation: Then, one emerges as Dveshavajra, with a body color of dark blue, and three faces—dark blue, white, and red—and six arms; the right hands hold a vajra, a wheel, and a lotus, and the left hands hold a bell, a jewel, and a sword, being embraced by the consort Sparshavajra who is similar to oneself. Both are adorned with the eight precious ornaments; the upper body is draped with a shawl of celestial fabric, and the lower body hangs with a skirt of celestial silk. Thus, one is generated in an instant. At one’s crown is Vairochana, at the throat Amitabha, at the heart Akshobhya (it is said to be important not to omit this), at the navel Ratnasambhava, and at the base of the thighs Amoghasiddhi. At the navel is Lochana, at the heart Mamaki, at the throat Pandaravasini, at the crown Tara, in the eyes Kshitigarbha, in the ears Vajrapani, in the nose Akashagarbha, on the tongue Avalokiteshvara, at the heart Manjushri, in the secret place Sarvanivaranavishkambhin, in the joints Kshitigarbha, and at the crown Maitreya. At the gate of the eyes is Rupavajra, at the gate of the ears Shabdavajra, at the gate of the nose Gandhavajra, at the gate of the mouth Rasavajra, and at the gate of the vajra Sparshavajra. In the right hand is Yamantaka, in the left hand Achala, at the mouth Hayagriva, at the vajra Amritakundali, at the base of the right shoulder Mi.g.yo.ba, at the base of the left shoulder Kamaraja, at the right knee Niladanda, at the left knee Mahabala, at the crown Ushnishachakravartin, and at the two soles of the feet Mahakrodha. Thus, the body mandala is arranged.

To attain buddhahood in a single lifetime, I am satisfied.

Through the Secret Mantra, which is rarer even than the Buddhas,
At this juncture of having encountered the Dharma by good fortune,

To attain buddhahood in a single lifetime, I am satisfied.
